analysis.time: The outbreak began in early October and no new cases have been reported since Oct.
analysis.location_and_population: Bentwood Elementary School in Olathe, Kansas, impacted 95 students and staff and 2 family members (N2).
analysis.event: An outbreak of norovirus was reported at Bentwood Elementary School, with two cases confirmed through laboratory testing and the rest epidemiologically linked (N3).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 95 cases among students and staff, 2 cases among family members. No hospitalizations were reported. Norovirus is highly contagious and frequently reported in school settings (N2, N7, N13).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Health officials and school authorities are monitoring the situation and working to prevent further spread. The outbreak is considered over, but ongoing surveillance is in place (N8, N9).

analysis.brief_en: A norovirus outbreak at Bentwood Elementary School in Olathe, Kansas, has impacted nearly 100 individuals, including 95 students and staff and two family members. Health officials confirmed two cases through laboratory testing, while the remaining were epidemiologically linked due to similar symptoms and timing. No hospitalizations were reported, and no new cases have emerged since October. Officials from the Johnson County Department of Health and Environment and Olathe Public Schools collaborated to monitor the outbreak, provide guidance, and prevent further spread. Although the outbreak is deemed over, continued surveillance is in place to ensure the health of students, staff, and families. Norovirus is a highly contagious virus that causes gastroenteritis, often spreading in close quarters like schools. The CDC notes it is the leading cause of foodborne illness in the U.S., with annual cases reaching around 21 million. Preventive measures include thorough handwashing with soap and water, as hand sanitizer is ineffective against the virus.
